label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: none

Mick, please don't go into 43 at 9, and Priya, please don't hand over a key yet. I know the offer is kindly meant.

I'm a chartered structural engineer, but I'm writing as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement at 7 this morning. This is not a survey and not professional advice.

What I saw: about 1.2m of the stack on 41 is still standing, leaning towards 43, with the mortar washed out at its base. Gusts of 50mph are forecast again this afternoon and it could come down at any time. The front roof of 43 has a hole of 2 to 3 square metres. A stepped crack 5 to 10mm wide runs from the top of the bay up to the first floor window cill, and the top of the bay looks to have dropped by about 20mm.

So the bay ceiling in 43 sits under a holed roof with a loose stack above it. That is the worst place anyone could stand. The floors may be loaded with fallen brickwork, and nobody knows at the moment how the weight above the bay is getting down to the ground. The same goes for looking at the loft from inside. Please leave it to the council's dangerous structures officer.

JoJo, your cousin isn't wrong that these terraces are robust in general. But that is true of an intact one, and this one is damaged.

Pavement: no, I wouldn't use it. There are loose slates along the gutter line of 43 and 45 directly over the footway, and the tape only goes across the front garden of 43. Please walk on the other side of the road until the council has been, especially on the school run. The council know about the house, but nobody has closed the footway. Out of hours, dangerous structures is reached through the main council number, so if you ring, tell them that.

Mrs Doherty: it isn't my decision. The front of 45 looks undamaged, and the stack sits on the wall between 41 and 43, not on her side. But I couldn't see the wall between 43 and 45 from the street. I would not sleep in the front room tonight, and I think it would be better if she went to family until 45 has been checked.

Ulrike
